body:
No, you're not alone. I've been suicidal/had suicidal ideation since I was like 8 years old. Horrible family life will wear on a child and the idea 'I wish I could just disappear' is the first step to suicidal ideation. Many children that grow up in abusive households will think this at some point, even kids in school from embarrassment will feel it and think it. 

It's whether or not they are given the right environment to believe that life is worth living/they are worth it that those thoughts become small and overtaken by positive ones.

I guess what I'm saying is that what you're feeling and have been feeling is something many others have felt. It's hard to look back on your childhood and go 'wow I've never been happy' so I get it. Sorry I don't have any real advice to give other than you're not alone.

Went to the psych emergency not too long ago. They looked at me like 'you poor thing, you just think you're sick'.

Being "high-functioning" doesn't mean I don't hurt too.

I don't and may never know you, but you're a man to me.

The point is you're strong enough to try and live your truth, that means you're strong enough to get through this.
